as-army-weights.statement: CBO's primary-metric weights — 0.40 protection and survivability, 0.30 lethality, 0.20 mobility, 0.10 passenger capacity — represent deployed soldiers' preferences well enough to rank the vehicles.

as-expert-estimates.statement: Army analysts' estimates for the Namer and the Puma are comparable with simulation results for the GCV and can be placed in the same table.

as-nine-squad.statement: Carrying a full nine-member squad in one vehicle materially improves the squad's effectiveness on dismount, and enough so that the secondary metric is right to score it all-or-nothing: 100 for a vehicle that carries nine, 0 for one that does not.

sc-conventional.description: Larger, more conventional battles against enemies equipped with armored vehicles, including a battalion-sized encounter in southwest Asia (p. 10 fn 12).
sc-conventional.name: Conventional armored battle

sc-ne-asia.description: The most intense battle CBO reports the Army simulating: a brigade-sized battle set in northeast Asia (p. 10 and fn 12).
sc-ne-asia.name: Northeast Asia intense battle

sc-unconventional.description: U.S. forces confronting unconventional threats and small numbers of combatants; CBO reports company-sized incidents in Iraq and Afghanistan among the simulated scenarios (p. 10 fn 12).
sc-unconventional.name: Unconventional threats

cl-cost.text: Fielding Pumas or upgraded Bradleys would cost $14 billion and $9 billion less, respectively, than the Army's GCV program over 2014 through 2030.

cl-primary.text: Under CBO's primary metric the Puma is the most capable of the five vehicles, followed by the upgraded Bradley IFV, the notional GCV and the Namer.

cl-secondary.text: Under CBO's secondary metric, which scores the nine-member squad all or nothing, the Puma stays slightly ahead of the GCV, and the Namer and the upgraded Bradley are within a quarter-point of each other — CBO printed both as 25.

cl-squad-rationale.text: The Army's stated reason for carrying a full nine-member squad in one vehicle is that a squad split between vehicles is hard to organise and direct in the moments after the soldiers dismount.

cl-weights.text: CBO's primary-metric weights are the Army's category weights for the four categories CBO could assess, renormalised to sum to one (CBO writes 'based on'; Table A-1's figures make it an exact renormalisation); the Army derived those from rankings given by soldiers who had deployed with combat brigades.
